name: Redness and visible vessels
summary: Visible vessels and persistent redness often reflect a sensitivity built up over many years, and they tend to become steadily more noticeable with age.
imageAlt: Skin with a pale line, close-up
statement: Visible vessels and persistent redness often reflect *a sensitivity built up over many years*, and they tend to become steadily more noticeable with age.
happening: Visible redness and small vessels usually reflect a combination of skin sensitivity, sun exposure and the natural thinning of skin over time. Some redness is constant; some appears in response to triggers such as heat or movement. The pattern helps determine which approach is likely to be most effective.

factors.title: Cumulative exposure
factors.text: Redness and visible vessels usually reflect cumulative exposure and skin behaviour over years, not a single recent cause.

factors.title: Barrier and turnover
factors.text: Changes to the skin barrier and cell turnover rate influence how visible redness and visible vessels become over time.

factors.title: Individual variation
factors.text: How redness and visible vessels present and respond to treatment varies meaningfully between skin types.

recommendedText: Considered as the primary option for visible redness and vessels, using light-based technology suited specifically to this concern.
alongsideText: Often assessed alongside, since these concerns frequently share the same treatment options.

steps.title: Assessment first
steps.text: We look at whether the redness is diffuse or comes from visible vessels, since each responds to a different approach.

steps.title: Barrier first
steps.text: Where skin is sensitive, its barrier is supported before light or laser treatment is considered.

steps.title: A course
steps.text: Redness usually settles over a series of sessions rather than a single treatment.

steps.title: Ongoing review
steps.text: Sensitivity can return, so the plan is reviewed at follow-up and adjusted as needed.
